{{short description|Dutch mathematician}}
[[File:Opdam eric.jpg|thumb|Opdam at [[Oberwolfach]], 2014]]
'''Eric Marcus Opdam''' (born 1960) is a Dutch mathematician, specializing in [[algebra]] and [[harmonic analysis]]. He is one of the two namesakes of [[Heckman–Opdam polynomials]].

Opdam received his PhD from [[Leiden University]] in 1988 under the supervision of [[Gerrit van Dijk (mathematician)|Gerrit van Dijk]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=62199}}</ref> Opdam is a professor at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. He has been at the [[Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics]] (KdVI) since 1999. From 2015 he is the KdVI's director as the successor to Jan Wiegerinck.<ref>[http://www.few.vu.nl/en/news-events/news-archive/2015/jan-mrt/eric-opdam-appointed-new-institute-director-of-kdvi.aspx Communication from the Free University of Amsterdam], 2015</ref>

Opdam's research deals with analytic aspects of [[Iwahori–Hecke algebra]]s, with hypergeometric functions associated with Lie algebra root systems (Heckman-Opdam hypergeometric functions), and with [[Dunkl operator]]s on complex reflection groups.

Opdam was an invited speaker in 2000 with talk ''Hecke algebras and harmonic analysis'' at the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in Barcelona. In 2006 he was an invited speaker at [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Madrid.<ref>{{cite book|author=Opdam, Eric M.|chapter=Hecke algebras and harmonic analysis|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians-Madrid|volume=2|pages=1227–1259|year=2006|chapter-url=https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/e.m.opdam/opdam.pdf}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/13817 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412094638/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/13817 |title=Eric Opdam |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=12 April 2020}}</ref> In 2010 he received an Advanced Grant from the [[European Research Council]] (ERC).

He is one of four managing editors of [[Compositio Mathematica]].
